sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Let's explore the world of true/false values in programming! Booleans are like light switches - they're either ON (true) or OFF (false).

• What boolean data types are and why they matter
• How to compare values using relational operators
• Where you'll use booleans in real code

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine you're at a traffic light. It's either RED (stop - false) or GREEN (go - true). That's exactly how booleans work in programming!

Booleans are the simplest data type - they can only be:
• `true` (yes, on, 1)
• `false` (no, off, 0)

They're perfect for answering yes/no questions like:
- Is the user logged in?
- Is the password correct?
- Has the game started?

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ Booleans are like light switches - only two states: true/false
✓ Relational operators (>, <, ==) always return boolean results
✓ Default boolean value is `false` if not initialized
✓ Used in conditions to control program flow
✓ Essential for flags, status checks, and decision making

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Initialize boolean variables when declaring them
Use `==` for equality comparison (not `=` which is assignment)
donts: Don't compare booleans with `== true` - just use the variable
Don't use numbers instead of booleans (0/1)
Don't forget that `!` flips the boolean value
sections.protip: Name your boolean variables as questions: `isReady`, `hasAccess`, `shouldUpdate` - this makes your code read like English!

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: Booleans are everywhere in real applications! Here's where you'll see them:

examples.how: Check if `isLoggedIn` is true before showing user dashboard
Use `hasDiscount` to apply promotions and `isInStock` to show 'Add to Cart'

sections.title: 🧪 Practice Problem
sections.content: Let's test your boolean skills! Write a program that checks if someone can ride a rollercoaster:

problem.description: A person can ride if they are at least 120cm tall AND at least 8 years old. Create variables for height and age, then determine if they can ride.
hints: Use the `&&` (AND) operator to combine conditions
Remember: both conditions must be true
Try different height/age values to test
problem.explanation: We combine two conditions with `&&` (AND). The result is only true when both height is ≥120 AND age is ≥8. This creates a single boolean that answers our question!

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 Booleans are simple true/false values that power decisions in code
📌 Relational operators compare values and return booleans
📌 Practice using them in conditions and flags
📌 You're ready to learn about if-statements next!
